required.quote: each optometrist shall be required to complete 20 hours of continuing education relating to optometry, as approved by the Board, each year.

hours_per_period.quote: each optometrist shall be required to complete 20 hours of continuing education relating to optometry, as approved by the Board, each year.

period_years.quote: each optometrist shall be required to complete 20 hours of continuing education relating to optometry, as approved by the Board, each year.

value: At least 10 hours through real-time, interactive activities (in-person or electronic presentations)
No more than 2 hours of recordkeeping/coding/practice management courses
For TPA-certified optometrists: at least 10 hours in ocular and general pharmacology, diagnosis and treatment, or new pharmaceutical agents, clinical devices, techniques, modalities, or procedures
topical_requirements.quote: Of the 20 hours of continuing education relating to optometry required pursuant to subsection A: 1. At least 10 hours shall be obtained through real-time, interactive activities... 2. No more than two hours may consist of courses related to recordkeeping... 3. For TPA-certified optometrists, at least 10 hours shall be in the areas of ocular and general pharmacology, diagnosis and treatment of the human eye and its adnexa...

available.quote: The regulatory boards may enter into agreements with other jurisdictions for the recognition of certificates and licenses issued by other jurisdictions.

requirements.value: Regulatory boards may enter agreements for recognition of out-of-state licenses; universal license recognition available if applicant holds current valid license in another state for at least 3 years, passed an examination, is in good standing, and has no disqualifying criminal record or discipline.
requirements.quote: the regulatory boards within the Department of Professional and Occupational Regulation shall, upon application by an individual, recognize licenses or certificates issued by another state as fulfillment of qualifications for licensure or government certification in the Commonwealth

national_certification.value: National Board of Examiners in Optometry (NBEO)

credential_type.quote: Every candidate successfully passing the examination shall be licensed by the Board if such candidate possesses the qualifications required by law and regulation to practice optometry.

is_mandatory.quote: It shall be unlawful for any person: 1. To practice optometry in this Commonwealth without holding a license issued by the Board.

title_protection.quote: Any person who in any way advertises himself as an optometrist or uses the title of doctor of optometry (O.D.) or any other letters or title in connection with his name which in any way conveys the impression that he is engaged in the practice of optometry shall be deemed to be practicing optometry within the meaning of this chapter.

scope_protection.quote: It shall be unlawful for any person: 1. To practice optometry in this Commonwealth without holding a license issued by the Board.

disciplinary_grounds.quote: Fraud or deceit in his practice;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Conviction of any felony or misdemeanor involving moral turpitude
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Conviction of any felony under the laws of the Commonwealth, another state, the District of Columbia, or any United States possession or territory or of any misdemeanor under such laws involving moral turpitude;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Conducting practice in a manner that endangers the health and welfare of patients or the public
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Conducting his practice in such a manner as to endanger the health and welfare of his patients or the public;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Use of alcohol or drugs to the extent rendering the optometrist unsafe to practice, or physical or mental illness rendering unsafe to practice
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Use of alcohol or drugs to the extent such use renders him unsafe to practice optometry or mental or physical illness rendering him unsafe to practice optometry;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Knowingly and willfully employing an unlicensed person to perform acts requiring an optometry license
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Knowingly and willfully employing an unlicensed person to do anything for which a license to practice optometry is required;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Neglecting or refusing to display the current year license
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Neglecting or refusing to display his license for the current year;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Obtaining fees by fraud, misrepresentation, deception, or fraud upon a patient
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Obtaining of any fee by fraud or misrepresentation or the practice of deception or fraud upon any patient;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Advertising that deceives, misleads, or defrauds the public, claims professional superiority, or offers free optometrical services or examinations
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Advertising that directly or indirectly deceives, misleads, or defrauds the public, claims professional superiority, or offers free optometrical services or examinations;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Employing, procuring, or inducing an unlicensed person to practice optometry
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Employing, procuring, or inducing a person not licensed to practice optometry to so practice;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Aiding or abetting the practice of optometry by any unlicensed person
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Aiding or abetting in the practice of optometry any person not duly licensed to practice in the Commonwealth;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Advertising, practicing, or attempting to practice optometry under a name other than one's own licensed name
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Advertising, practicing, or attempting to practice optometry under a name other than one's own name as set forth on the license;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Lending, leasing, renting, or placing license at the disposal of an unlicensed person
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Lending, leasing, renting, or in any other manner placing his license at the disposal or in the service of any person not licensed to practice optometry in the Commonwealth;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Splitting or dividing fees with anyone other than a licensed optometrist who is a legal partner or co-member of a professional LLC
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Splitting or dividing a fee with any person or persons other than with a licensed optometrist who is a legal partner or comember of a professional limited liability company formed to engage in the practice of optometry;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Practicing optometry where an officer, employee, or agent of a commercial or mercantile establishment (not licensed as an optometrist or physician) controls professional judgment
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Practicing optometry where any officer, employee, or agent of a commercial or mercantile establishment, as defined in subsection C of § 54.1-3205, who is not licensed in the Commonwealth to practice optometry or medicine directly or indirectly controls, dictates, or influences the professional judgment, including but not limited to the level or type of care or services rendered, of the licensed optometrist;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violating other standards of conduct adopted by the Board
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Violating other standards of conduct as adopted by the Board;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violating, assisting, inducing, or cooperating with others in violating any provisions of law or regulations relating to the practice of optometry
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Violating, assisting, inducing, or cooperating with others in violating any provisions of law relating to the practice of optometry, including the provisions of this chapter or of any regulation of the Board.

definition_quote.value: The practice of optometry includes: Examination of the human eye to ascertain the presence of defects or abnormal conditions; Employment of any subjective or objective mechanism to determine the accommodative or refractive states; Use of testing appliances; Examination, diagnosis, and optometric treatment; Evaluation, examination, diagnosis, and treatment of abnormal or diseased conditions of the human eye and its adnexa; Preoperative and postoperative care; and Use of diagnostic pharmaceutical agents.
definition_quote.quote: The practice of optometry includes: 1. Examination of the human eye to ascertain the presence of defects or abnormal conditions that may be corrected or relieved by the use of lenses, prisms or ocular exercises, or visual training or orthoptics and the prescribing or adapting of lenses, prisms or ocular exercises, or visual training or orthoptics for the correction, relief, remediation, or prevention of such conditions

value: examination and diagnosis of the human eye
prescribing and adapting lenses, prisms, or ocular exercises
visual training or orthoptics
use of subjective or objective mechanisms to determine refractive states
use of testing appliances
optometric treatment of conditions and visual or muscular anomalies
evaluation and treatment of abnormal or diseased conditions of the human eye and adnexa
preoperative and postoperative care
use of diagnostic pharmaceutical agents
treatment with therapeutic pharmaceutical agents (TPA-certified)
intramuscular epinephrine for anaphylactic shock
laser surgery (peripheral iridotomy, selective laser trabeculoplasty, YAG capsulotomy) if certified
methods_authorized.quote: The practice of optometry includes: 1. Examination of the human eye... 2. Employment of any subjective or objective mechanism... 3. Use of testing appliances... 4. Examination, diagnosis, and optometric treatment... 5. Evaluation, examination, diagnosis, and treatment of abnormal or diseased conditions... 6. Preoperative and postoperative care... 7. Use of diagnostic pharmaceutical agents

drug_authority.value: TPA-certified optometrists may prescribe and administer Schedule II (hydrocodone/acetaminophen combination), Schedules III-VI controlled substances to treat diseases of the human eye and adnexa; diagnostic pharmaceutical agents (Schedule VI) by topical application for all licensed optometrists after June 30, 1997; intramuscular epinephrine for anaphylaxis; steroid injection for chalazia (TPA-certified only).
drug_authority.quote: TPA certification shall enable an optometrist to prescribe and administer, within his scope of practice, Schedule II controlled substances consisting of hydrocodone in combination with acetaminophen and Schedules III through VI controlled substances and devices as set forth in the Drug Control Act

surgery_prohibited.quote: Except as provided in §§ 54.1-3222 and 54.1-3225, the practice of optometry does not include treatment through: 1. Surgery, including: a. Retina laser procedures; laser procedures into the vitreous chamber of the eye... laser in situ keratomileusis and photorefractive keratectomy eye surgery; or other laser surgery

surgery_definition.value: Surgery means the structural alteration of the human body by the incision or cutting into of tissue for the purpose of diagnostic or therapeutic treatment of conditions or disease processes by any instrument causing localized alteration or transposition of live human tissue, but does not include procedures for the removal of superficial foreign bodies, punctures, injections, dry needling, acupuncture, or removal of dead tissue.
surgery_definition.quote: "surgery" means the structural alteration of the human body by the incision or cutting into of tissue for the purpose of diagnostic or therapeutic treatment of conditions or disease processes by any instrument causing localized alteration or transposition of live human tissue, but does not include the following: procedures for the removal of superficial foreign bodies from the human body, punctures, injections, dry needling, acupuncture, or removal of dead tissue.

foreign_body_removal_authorized.quote: The foregoing shall not restrict the authority of any optometrist licensed or certified under this chapter for the removal of superficial foreign bodies from the human eye and its adnexa

value: peripheral iridotomy
selective laser trabeculoplasty
YAG capsulotomy
laser_procedures_authorized.quote: The Board shall certify an optometrist to perform laser surgery consisting of peripheral iridotomy, selective laser trabeculoplasty, and YAG capsulotomy for the medically appropriate and recognized treatment of the human eye

value: injection of steroid (Schedule VI) for treatment of chalazia
minor_surgical_procedures_authorized.quote: Administration of therapeutic pharmaceutical agents by injection shall be limited to the treatment of chalazia by means of injection of a steroid included in Schedule VI controlled substances

glaucoma_treatment_authorized.quote: Treatment of angle closure glaucoma shall be limited to initiation of immediate emergency care.

anaphylaxis_treatment_authorized.quote: administer intramuscular epinephrine for the treatment of emergency cases of anaphylactic shock.

vision_therapy_authorized.quote: the use of lenses, prisms or ocular exercises, or visual training or orthoptics and the prescribing or adapting of lenses, prisms or ocular exercises, or visual training or orthoptics for the correction, relief, remediation, or prevention of such conditions

value: Schedule II limited to hydrocodone in combination with acetaminophen only (no other Schedule II substances)
Treatment of infantile or congenital glaucoma prohibited
Oral TPAs limited to analgesics on Schedule II (hydrocodone/acetaminophen) and Schedules III-VI, and other Schedule VI substances appropriate to treat eye diseases
controlled_substance_schedule_restrictio.quote: Treatment with oral therapeutic pharmaceutical agents shall be limited to (i) analgesics included on Schedule II controlled substances as defined in § 54.1-3448 of the Drug Control Act consisting of hydrocodone in combination with acetaminophen, and analgesics included on Schedules III through VI... Treatment of infantile or congenital glaucoma shall be prohibited.

oral_pharmaceutical_authority.quote: Treatment with oral therapeutic pharmaceutical agents shall be limited to (i) analgesics included on Schedule II controlled substances as defined in § 54.1-3448 of the Drug Control Act consisting of hydrocodone in combination with acetaminophen, and analgesics included on Schedules III through VI, as defined in §§ 54.1-3450 and 54.1-3455 of the Drug Control Act, which are appropriate to alleviate ocular pain and (ii) other Schedule VI controlled substances as defined in § 54.1-3455 of the Drug Control Act appropriate to treat diseases and abnormal conditions of the human eye and its adnexa.

pharmaceutical_certification_required.quote: "TPA-certified optometrist" means an optometrist who is licensed under this chapter and who has successfully completed the requirements for TPA certification established by the Board pursuant to Article 5 (§ 54.1-3222 et seq.).

value: optometrist (basic license)
TPA-certified optometrist
optometrist certified to perform laser surgery
tiered_license_types.quote: "TPA-certified optometrist" means an optometrist who is licensed under this chapter and who has successfully completed the requirements for TPA certification established by the Board pursuant to Article 5 (§ 54.1-3222 et seq.).

value: TPA certification (therapeutic pharmaceutical agents)
laser surgery certification (peripheral iridotomy, selective laser trabeculoplasty, YAG capsulotomy)
specialty_certification_types.quote: The Board shall certify an optometrist to perform laser surgery consisting of peripheral iridotomy, selective laser trabeculoplasty, and YAG capsulotomy

supervised_clinical_internship_required.quote: A TPA-certified optometrist shall provide written evidence to the Board that he has completed a didactic and clinical training course provided by an accredited school or college of optometry that includes training in administration of TPAs by injection prior to administering TPAs by injection pursuant to this subdivision.

delegation_to_unlicensed_assistants_auth.quote: delegating to personnel in his personal employ and supervised by him, such activities or functions as are nondiscretionary and do not require the exercise of professional judgment for their performance and which are usually or customarily delegated to such persons by optometrists, if such activities or functions are authorized by and performed for such optometrists and responsibility for such activities or functions is assumed by such optometrists.

impaired_practitioner_program_establishe.quote: To establish, and revise as necessary, a health practitioners' monitoring program pursuant to Chapter 25.1 (§ 54.1-2515 et seq.);
impaired_practitioner_program_establishe.citation: UMBRELLA / Chapter 25 - Department of Health Professions

criminal_background_check_required.quote: A regulatory board may require any applicant for registration, licensure, or certification to submit to fingerprinting and to provide personal descriptive information to be forwarded along with the applicant's fingerprints through the Central Criminal Records Exchange to the Federal Bureau of Investigation for the purpose of obtaining criminal history record information regarding such applicant.
